title: Mud-brick houses
description: Common Sumerian dwellings were rectangular mud-brick houses with flat roofs, often two stories with a central courtyard

title: Barley bread and beer
description: Barley was the staple grain; bread and beer were consumed daily by all social classes

title: Scribal training
description: Young boys from elite families attended edubba (tablet house) schools to learn cuneiform writing

title: Workers village at Deir el-Medina
description: Artisan families lived in small stone houses along narrow streets in planned worker communities

title: Linen garments
description: Egyptians wore white linen clothing; elites had finely pleated garments while commoners wore simpler wraps

title: Public baths
description: Romans of all classes visited public bathhouses (thermae) for bathing, socializing, and exercise

title: Cena (main meal)
description: The main Roman meal was eaten in late afternoon; elites reclined on couches for elaborate multi-course dinners

title: Forum marketplace
description: Daily commerce centered on the forum, where merchants sold food, pottery, textiles, and other goods

title: Confucian studies
description: Elite young men studied the Five Classics and practiced calligraphy as preparation for government service

title: Bathing rituals
description: Regular bathing was expected; officials received a day off every five days specifically for bathing

title: Woolen tunics and cloaks
description: Vikings wore layered woolen clothing with linen undergarments; brooches indicated social status

title: Seasonal farming and raiding
description: Free men alternated between farming in summer and trading or raiding voyages in warmer months

title: Market day at Tlatelolco
description: The great market operated daily, with 60,000 people trading goods regulated by market judges

title: Maize tortillas and tamales
description: Maize was prepared as tortillas, tamales, and atole (porridge); chocolate was reserved for elites

title: Kabuki theater
description: Townspeople flocked to kabuki performances in licensed theater districts as popular entertainment
